To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adult hippocampus maintains the rules of neuronal differentiation that are observed in embryonic development, and that these rules are not observed in the olfaction system.
1) neuronal differentiation occurs in an adult brain area, the hippocampus, and 2) the sequence of neuronal connectivity during development is recapitulated in the adult brain.
“In the adult hippocampus neural progenitors give rise to new granule cells that develop through the same sequence of synaptic connectivity as in embryonic development.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neuronal differentiation, migration and synaptic integration in the adult brain.
the mechanisms that control the generation, migration, and integration of new neurons in the adult brain.
the development, maintenance and repair of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hippocampus, like the embryonic hippocampus, is not a plastic brain structure but rather a rigid one, with a very strict and precise developmental program that cannot be changed by the environment.
the hippocampus maintains a developmental sequence for integration through adulthood.
the hippocampus maintains developmental rules for neuronal differentiation through adulthood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the adult brain, neurons are born and then mature in the same way as in embryonic development.

in the hippocampus, the developmental rules for the maturation and integration of new neurons are the same in adults as in the embryo, whereas in the olfactory system, the developmental rules are different in adults than in the embryo.

in the adult hippocampal neurogenesis process, the first step is that the newborn neuron migrates to the granule cell (GC) layer, then it becomes silent for a while and then it starts to receive slow GABAergic input, and finally it becomes mature, with fast GABAergic and glutamatergics inputs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the adult brain is capable of generating new neurons throughout life, these new neurons do not functionally integrate into pre-existing circuits in the same way that embryonic neurons do.

neuronal differentiation in the adult hippocampal neurogenic niches follows a developmental program similar to the embryonic one, which suggests that the same mechanisms are at play during both developmental periods.
the adult hippocampus has the ability to generate neurons with the same functional properties as neurons that are generated during embryonic development.
